description: Use this when the signed-in clipper asks to cut, make or download clips, for example "cut clips 1 to 3" after the creative plan numbered them. ClippingAlpha's server cuts each clip from the campaign's source video into a vertical 1080 by 1920 MP4 with captions burned in, the brief's #ad on screen when it asks for one, and loudness levelled. Takes the clip numbers of the campaign's creative plan, brand clips included, or a source_id with a start and end in seconds. It cuts the footage the campaign gives its clippers, as the signed-in answers list it: the YouTube, Twitch, Kick, TikTok, Instagram and X videos it links and its brand files (Google Drive, Dropbox, Frame.io, WeTransfer, OneDrive, Egnyte, the Evangelist media library), the footage its clipping platform gives the clippers who join included. Never an upload or a video ClippingAlpha has not read. Up to 5 clips a call and 10 a day, within a daily clip limit per clipper and a daily total for all clipping. A refused call says when the limit resets and uses none of it. Answers at once with the clip ids. The download links follow when the clips are ready, usually within a minute or two. Each link works for 24 hours. Needs the clipper's ClippingAlpha sign-in. Nothing is posted anywhere. The clipper asks for the cut for their own work on the campaign and is responsible for using it within the campaign's, the brand's and the platforms' rules (clippingalpha.com/terms#terms-clips).

app.description: Set only by the ClippingAlpha app in the chat, to count its steps. Leave it out.

campaign.description: The campaign as brand/series, its page URL or its campaignId.

clips.description: The clip numbers of the campaign's creative plan, for example [1, 2, 3].

ranges.description: Or exact ranges of the campaign's videos or brand files.

end_sec.description: Where it ends, 3 seconds to 3 minutes after the start.

source_id.description: The sourceId of one of the campaign's videos or brand files, as an earlier signed-in answer gave it.

start_sec.description: Where the clip starts, in seconds of the source.
